meta_description:
3,181 likes, 43 comments - suyashkeshari on October 4, 2026: "Have you ever seen a tiger hugging a tree?🌳🐯 

This is a big male scratch marking a tree @ameliyasafaris 

This is a form of territorial marking and communication. 

Tigers have scent glands between their toes, so when they scratch, they leave behind both a visual message and their scent.

Other tigers can then pick up on these marks and scents, helping them understand who has been through the area and that the territory is occupied.

And the higher and more prominent the scratch marks, the harder they are to miss. It also signals dominance. 

So while we put up signs saying “Private Property”…

Tigers scratch a tree 🐅

Same message. Much better handwriting. 😜

#TigerSafariIndia #bandhavgarh #luxurysafari #indiansafari".
